channel.title: PsyDigest — psychiatry literature digest
channel.description: Summaries of new psychiatric research and guidelines

item.title: The effectiveness of digital therapeutics in improving sleep quality: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A network meta-analysis evaluated the comparative effectiveness of six digital therapeutics for insomnia across 96 randomized controlled trials.
FINDINGS: Digital cognitive behavioral therapy (dCBT) showed the most robust evidence, with a moderate-certainty reduction in Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) scores (MD: -4.24 points) and low-certainty improvements in other sleep parameters. Digital mindfulness-based therapy (dMBT) and virtual reality (VR) showed some benefits, but only dCBT reached the minimal clinically important difference (MCID). Other digital therapeutics (dBBT, CRS, NFB) showed no significant effects.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: dCBT is the most effective digital therapeutic for insomnia, but clinical significance for other modalities remains uncertain.

item.title: Comparative efficacy of antipsychotics for reducing aggression in schizophrenia: systematic review and network meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A systematic review and network meta-analysis compared the efficacy of different antipsychotics for reducing aggression in adults with schizophrenia.
FINDINGS: In 41 RCTs (n=21,025), clozapine (SMD −0.75), paliperidone (−0.62) and olanzapine (−0.60) showed the largest reductions in aggression versus placebo; smaller effects were seen with asenapine, risperidone, aripiprazole and haloperidol. Median follow-up was 8 weeks and overall confidence in the evidence was low to very low due to bias and incoherence.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clozapine, paliperidone and olanzapine may be considered when aggression is a treatment priority, but the low certainty of evidence warrants cautious interpretation and shared decision-making.

item.title: Comparing lithium and valproate in reducing suicide risk: A territory-wide retrospective cohort study with pairwise and network meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A territory-wide retrospective cohort study combined with meta-analyses compared lithium and valproate for suicide prevention in bipolar disorder.
FINDINGS: In the cohort (n=6 935), suicide risk did not differ between lithium and valproate (HR 0.76, 95 % CI 0.54–1.08). Pairwise meta-analysis of eight observational studies likewise showed no significant difference (HR 0.87, 95 % CI 0.69–1.09). Network meta-analysis suggested both agents lowered suicide risk versus no treatment (lithium HR 0.46, valproate HR 0.63), but they were not significantly different from each other (HR 0.73, 95 % CI 0.52–1.02).
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Lithium and valproate appear similarly effective for suicide prevention in bipolar disorder; selection should be individualized based on patient profile and tolerability.

item.title: 2026 EASD evidence-based clinical practice guideline for assessing and managing diabetes distress among adults with type 1 diabetes or type 2 diabetes.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This 2026 EASD guideline provides evidence-based recommendations for assessing and managing diabetes distress in adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
FINDINGS: The guideline recommends routine screening for diabetes distress using validated tools, with eight Good Practice Statements emphasizing ongoing monitoring and collaborative care. For type 1 diabetes, conditional recommendations support psychological interventions, continuous glucose monitoring, and automated insulin delivery systems. For type 2 diabetes, psychological, psychoeducational, and educational interventions are conditionally recommended. Recommendations are based on GRADE methodology and systematic reviews of RCTs, though evidence quality is limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians should integrate validated distress screening and person-centered interventions into diabetes care, acknowledging evidence gaps and the need for system-level support.

item.title: Non-pharmacological interventions for opioid use disorder: protocol for a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) are being evaluated for their role in managing opioid use disorder (OUD), but high-quality comparative evidence remains limited.
FINDINGS: This systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) will synthesize randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing NPIs (e.g., behavioral therapies, psychosocial support) against standard pharmacological care or alternative NPIs in adults with OUD. Outcomes include abstinence, craving, treatment retention, relapse rates, and mental health measures, with effect modifiers such as pharmacological background and treatment duration explored via meta-regression.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This NMA aims to provide an evidence-based hierarchy of NPIs to guide individualized treatment decisions in OUD, pending the results of the analysis.

item.title: Why did antidepressant deprescribing fail? A scoping review of contributing factors.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A scoping review examined why antidepressant deprescribing interventions in primary care often fail despite rising long-term use.
FINDINGS: Nine studies (mostly RCTs) showed short tapering schedules, moderate-to-low protocol adherence, and high relapse rates, with general practitioners leading most efforts. Cohort studies using gradual tapering reported higher discontinuation rates, but no trials included structured interprofessional collaboration or patient involvement.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Deprescribing strategies may need longer, adaptive tapering and better multidisciplinary coordination to improve outcomes.

item.title: Project Harmony 2.0: protocol for an updated and expanded individual patient data meta-analysis and virtual clinical trial of treatments for comorbid PTSD and substance use disorders.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Comorbid PTSD and substance use disorders (PTSD + SUD) are common, but comparative treatment effectiveness remains unclear due to methodological limitations in prior research.
FINDINGS: This study will harmonize data from over 60 RCTs (N > 8,000) to compare pharmacological, behavioral, and combination treatments for PTSD + SUD using advanced methods (individual patient data meta-analysis, integrative data analysis, and propensity score weighting). Outcomes include latent PTSD severity, substance use, psychosocial functioning, and recovery indicators, with clinically significant change (CSC) assessed in the original dataset (36 RCTs; N = 4,046).
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This large-scale analysis aims to identify the most effective treatments for PTSD + SUD, potentially guiding personalized clinical decision-making.

item.title: Psychosocial interventions for posttraumatic stress disorder in low- and middle-income countries: a Bayesian meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Psychosocial interventions for PTSD in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) have lacked comprehensive synthesis despite high prevalence.
FINDINGS: A Bayesian meta-analysis of 55 RCTs (n=5,041) found large within-group (g = -1.88) and between-group (g = -1.31) effects for PTSD symptoms at post-assessment, sustained at follow-up, with medium-to-large effects for depression and anxiety. Trauma-focused, face-to-face interventions in older participants showed greater efficacy.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Trauma-focused psychosocial interventions should be prioritized as first-line treatments for PTSD in LMICs, though more high-quality research is needed.

item.title: The 2025 revision of JPOS/JASCC clinical guidelines for delirium in adult patients with cancer: a summary of recommendations.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The Japan Psycho-Oncology Society and the Japanese Association of Supportive Care in Cancer updated their 2025 clinical guidelines for delirium in adult cancer patients.
FINDINGS: Multicomponent interventions were strongly recommended for delirium prevention (moderate-certainty evidence), while bright light therapy, antipsychotics, ramelteon, and orexin receptor antagonists were not recommended. For management, antipsychotics, trazodone, and opioid switching were suggested, but benzodiazepines alone or combined with antipsychotics/antihistamines were not recommended; all management recommendations were weak with low to very-low certainty.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These guidelines provide a practical, evidence-based framework for delirium prevention and management in oncology settings, though high-quality evidence remains limited.

item.title: Effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy for postpartum depression: a systematic review and meta‑analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common condition affecting 17.22% of women globally, and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) is a recommended treatment, though its efficacy across delivery formats remains uncertain.
FINDINGS: A meta-analysis of eight RCTs (n=1,811) found CBT significantly reduced EPDS scores (SMD = -0.59) and increased clinical improvement rates (RR = 1.84). It may also improve social support and reduce anxiety, but showed no effect on infant temperament.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: CBT is effective for PPD but evidence certainty varies, and further research is needed on accessible delivery models.

item.title: Pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions of insomnia in geriatrics: A systematic review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Insomnia is highly prevalent in older adults, but treatment is complicated by age-related risks and polypharmacy.
FINDINGS: A systematic review and meta-analysis (22 RCTs) found dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs) had the best efficacy-safety balance for sleep initiation (sTSO SMD -0.28, 95% CI -0.41 to -0.15), while benzodiazepines/Z-drugs increased fall risk (RR ~1.47). Face-to-face CBT-I improved sleep efficiency (MD +8.36%) and reduced wake time (MD -23.44 min), though heterogeneity was high.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: CBT-I remains first-line for geriatric insomnia, with DORAs as the safest pharmacological option if medication is required.

item.title: Long-Term Psychodynamic Psychotherapy for Depression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy (LTPP) for depression in randomized controlled trials.
FINDINGS: At treatment completion, LTPP significantly reduced depressive symptoms compared to all comparators (SMD = 0.34, 95% CI [0.20, 0.47]) and active treatments specifically (SMD = 0.27, 95% CI [0.1, 0.45]), with effects generally sustained at follow-up. Effects were larger when compared to active controls (SMD = 0.61), but evidence quality was very low. GRADE assessments indicated high-certainty evidence for depressive symptom outcomes overall and moderate-certainty evidence in comparisons with active treatments.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: LTPP may be considered for patients with depression, particularly when other treatments have been ineffective, though evidence for functional outcomes and cost-effectiveness remains limited.

item.title: A systematic review of clinical practice guidelines for suicide and self-harm prevention in adults.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review evaluated the quality and content of clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for suicide and self-harm prevention in adults.
FINDINGS: Of 22 included guidelines (2000–2024), 13 were high-quality (AGREE-II ≥60% in ≥3 domains), but only 3 addressed implementation (Applicability domain). High-quality guidelines consistently recommended psychosocial assessment, aftercare planning, means restriction, and caution against sole reliance on risk-calculation tools.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: High-quality CPGs provide structured, evidence-informed care pathways for suicide/self-harm management, though better implementation strategies are needed.

item.title: [Clinical practice guideline for digital smoking cessation technologies (2026 edition)].
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A 2026 clinical practice guideline systematically synthesizes evidence on digital smoking-cessation technologies and issues eight graded recommendations for smokers ≥15 years intending to quit.
FINDINGS: Three strong recommendations endorse smartphone apps (1C), combined use of SMS/WeChat, apps and AI systems with standard therapies (1B–1C), and integrated “online-plus-offline” platforms (1C). Five conditional recommendations suggest supportive roles for SMS/WeChat (2B), web-based modules (2D), AI systems (2B), theory-driven, interactive tools (2C), and routine safety monitoring (2C).
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The guideline provides an evidence-based framework for integrating digital cessation tools into routine care while emphasizing safety and phased personalization.

item.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Lithium- Vs. Valproate-Based Combinations With Atypical Antipsychotics in Preventing Rehospitalization After a First Manic Episode of Bipolar I Disorder.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A first manic episode in bipolar I disorder often leads to relapse and rehospitalization, but head-to-head evidence comparing lithium- versus valproate-based maintenance regimens is lacking.
FINDINGS: In a propensity score–matched cohort of 3,909 Taiwanese patients discharged after their first mania hospitalization, valproate plus atypical antipsychotics (Val + AAPs) was associated with a lower risk of any mood-episode rehospitalization than lithium plus AAPs (HR 1.18, 95 % CI 1.03–1.35), driven mainly by fewer manic relapses (HR 1.16, 95 % CI 1.01–1.35); annualized rehospitalization rates were also higher with Li + AAPs (IRR 1.34, 95 % CI 1.17–1.54).
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: For patients recently hospitalized for a first manic episode, valproate-based combinations may offer a modest early-maintenance advantage over lithium-based combinations in preventing rehospitalization.

item.title: Sex differences in the efficacy, acceptability, and tolerability of antipsychotics in people with acute schizophrenia: individual participant data pairwise, dose-response, and network meta-analyses.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This large individual participant data meta-analysis assessed whether antipsychotic efficacy, acceptability, and tolerability differ between females and males with acute schizophrenia.
FINDINGS: In 18 fixed-dose trials (n=7062), no sex differences were found in overall symptom reduction (DoSMD 0.04, 95% CI -0.09 to 0.18). Antipsychotics reduced all-cause dropout more in females than males (ratio of odds ratios 0.74, 95% CI 0.56–0.98), and prolactin increases were greater in females (DoSMD 0.83, 95% CI 0.67–0.99). No clear sex-specific dose-response or network meta-analysis effects were observed.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current efficacy estimates for antipsychotics appear broadly applicable to both sexes, though clinicians should monitor prolactin elevations and dropout risk more closely in females.

item.title: Designing Youth Early Intervention in Psychosis Services: A Secondary Framework Synthesis of Organisational Recommendations.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: International guidance documents on early intervention in psychosis (EIP) provide organisational recommendations, but their synthesis and practical translation into service structures remain uneven.
FINDINGS: A secondary framework synthesis of 26 international guidance documents found strong consensus on specialised multidisciplinary services for CHR-P (16/17 documents) and dedicated EIP teams for FEP (20/22 documents). Coordination and continuity of care were also frequently recommended, while access arrangements and youth-friendly contexts were less consistently operationalised.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The framework highlights key organisational priorities for EIP service design, though some domains require clearer operational guidance for implementation.

item.title: Acute Effects of Brief Exercise on Alcohol Craving Among Young Adults With Problematic Alcohol Use: A Systematic Review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A systematic review examined whether brief exercise reduces alcohol craving in young adults with problematic alcohol use.
FINDINGS: Meta-analysis of six studies (n≈200) found a moderate short-term reduction in craving after a single exercise session (Hedges’ g ≈ 0.55) with moderate heterogeneity; narrative data suggested concurrent reductions in anxiety and stress markers.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: A single bout of exercise may offer a short-term adjunct to help curb craving in young adults with problematic alcohol use, pending more rigorous trials.

item.title: Cannabis use is associated with increased risk of violence: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Cannabis use is frequently linked to adverse mental health outcomes, but its specific association with violence remains uncertain.
FINDINGS: A meta-analysis of 63 studies (N = 265,079) found that cannabis users have a significantly higher risk of perpetrating violence, with odds ratios (ORs) of 2.49 in psychiatric patients and 2.05 in the general population. The association was stronger for violence involving criminal convictions (ORs 3.75–4.21) and also showed an increased risk of victimization (OR 1.49), particularly among females.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Routine assessment of cannabis use may be warranted in psychiatric settings to identify individuals at higher risk of violence or victimization.

item.title: Research trends in olanzapine in treating schizophrenia from 2010 to 2026: A bibliometric analysis based on the Web of Science Core Collection.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A bibliometric analysis examined global research trends on olanzapine for schizophrenia from 2010 to 2026.
FINDINGS: 3,943 publications were identified, with rising annual output; the US, China, and UK led contributions. Research focus evolved from efficacy to metabolic risk, personalized dosing, and real-world studies, with recent emphasis on cohort designs and guideline development.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The shift toward safety monitoring and individualized care underscores the need for clinicians to prioritize metabolic risk management in olanzapine-treated patients.

item.title: Zuclopenthixol acetate for acute schizophrenia and similar major mental illnesses.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Zuclopenthixol acetate, an intramuscular antipsychotic, is used for rapid tranquillisation in acute behavioural disturbance, but its comparative efficacy and tolerability remain uncertain.
FINDINGS: This Cochrane review (11 RCTs, n=714) found low-to-moderate certainty evidence suggesting no clear advantage of zuclopenthixol acetate over standard treatments (e.g., haloperidol + promethazine) for tranquillisation or global symptom improvement. Sedation was less at 15 minutes with zuclopenthixol acetate but greater at 24–48 hours (RR 0.25–0.62). Adjunctive benzodiazepine use was lower with zuclopenthixol acetate in one study (RR 0.03), but evidence was very uncertain. Dose comparisons (25–50 mg vs. 50–100 mg) showed no meaningful differences.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Zuclopenthixol acetate may offer no clear clinical benefit over standard rapid tranquillisation strategies, though its prolonged sedation could be advantageous in specific cases.

item.title: QTc changes and early major adverse cardiovascular events associated with antidepressant treatment for major depressive disorder in adults: individual participant data network meta-regression of double blind randomised trials.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This study compared the effects of specific antidepressants on QTc prolongation and early major cardiovascular adverse events (MACE) in adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) using individual participant data (IPD) from double-blind randomized trials.
FINDINGS: Escitalopram and amitriptyline were associated with increased QTc intervals (8.7 ms and 5.3 ms, respectively) compared to placebo, with variability in effects across drugs. No association was found between antidepressant use and early MACE or non-suicidal sudden death (risk difference 0.01%, 95% CrI -0.01% to 0.02%). Risk factors such as baseline QTc, age, and renal function influenced QTc changes.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians should consider individual cardiovascular risk factors when selecting antidepressants, particularly for drugs like escitalopram and amitriptyline, but no increased early MACE risk was observed.

item.title: Therapeutic alliance across delivery modalities: a systematic narrative review of alliance strength and outcome prediction in face-to-face, online, and blended psychotherapy.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A systematic narrative review examined whether therapeutic alliance (TA) strength and its association with outcomes differ across face-to-face (FTF), online, and blended psychotherapy modalities.
FINDINGS: Nine studies (including three RCTs) showed broadly comparable TA strength across FTF, pure online (PO: videoconference, telephone, asynchronous), and blended (BLD) modalities. One study reported lower patient-rated TA at Week 2 in asynchronous PO vs. FTF, but this resolved by Week 8. The TA–outcome association was less consistent in PO/BLD than in FTF.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Therapeutic alliance appears largely similar across delivery formats, though asynchronous online therapy may require early attention to alliance formation.

item.title: Polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) supplementation and ADHD outcomes in children and adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) supplementation, particularly omega-3 fatty acids, has been proposed as an adjunctive treatment for ADHD due to concerns about medication side effects and variable treatment responses.
FINDINGS: A meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials found a small, borderline statistically significant improvement in ADHD outcomes with PUFA supplementation (Hedges' g = -0.24, 95% CI -0.48 to -0.00), with substantial heterogeneity. Effects were stronger on performance-based cognitive assessments than on subjective behavioral ratings, and no clear dose-duration relationship was observed.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: PUFA supplementation may offer modest, context-dependent benefits as an adjunctive treatment for ADHD but is unlikely to replace standard therapies.

item.title: A multidisciplinary perspective on digital health interventions in schizophrenia care: Expanding the 2026 Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations guidelines.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This paper synthesizes recent evidence on digital health interventions (DHIs) for schizophrenia care from a multidisciplinary and lived-experience perspective.
FINDINGS: Evidence from RCTs suggests DHIs can improve specific psychotic symptoms, cognition, and reduce relapse risk, with growing acceptability and feasibility. However, no RCTs yet target physical health comorbidities, though co-designed interventions show promise. The overall evidence base is expanding but remains limited in scope and quality.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: DHIs with established efficacy should be considered adjunctive treatments in schizophrenia care, provided safety, accessibility, and implementation are prioritized.

item.title: Machine learning methods and schizophrenia spectrum disorders: a scoping review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly explored as a tool to address the heterogeneity of schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSDs) in diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment.
FINDINGS: A scoping review of 88 studies found ML applications across five domains: clinical (e.g., relapse, suicide risk), treatment (e.g., clozapine response), functional (e.g., speech analysis), behavioral (e.g., aggression), and provider outcomes (e.g., prescribing patterns). Most studies were cross-sectional (n=62), with moderate methodological quality (mean APPRAISE-AI score 47.4/100). Advanced techniques like deep learning and multimodal data integration were common, but clinical validation remains limited.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: ML may enhance individualized care in SSD, but rigorous validation and interpretability are needed before routine clinical adoption.

item.title: Peripheral Inflammatory Biomarkers as Predictors of Antidepressant Treatment Response in Major Depressive Disorder: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether baseline peripheral inflammatory biomarkers predict antidepressant response in adults with major depressive disorder (MDD).
FINDINGS: Across 24 studies, no baseline biomarker consistently differentiated responders from non-responders in pooled analyses. However, in recent studies (2021–2026), lower baseline IL-2 (SMD = -0.81) and IL-6 (SMD = -0.37) were nominally associated with better response, particularly for SSRIs/SNRIs.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not support routine use of peripheral inflammatory biomarkers to predict antidepressant response, though IL-2 and IL-6 may warrant further investigation in specific contexts.

item.title: Weight Gain During SSRI Therapy: The Potential Role of the Gut Microbiota-A Narrative Review and Mechanistic Hypothesis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: SSRIs, first-line treatments for depression, are associated with weight gain, potentially linked to gut microbiota alterations.
FINDINGS: Experimental and clinical studies suggest SSRIs may modify gut microbiota composition and function, influencing metabolites like short-chain fatty acids and bile acids, which could affect appetite and energy balance. Dietary interventions (e.g., fiber, Mediterranean diet, probiotics) may modulate these pathways, but no RCTs have tested their efficacy in preventing SSRI-related weight gain.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Gut microbiota may play a role in SSRI-induced weight gain, but evidence is preliminary and requires direct clinical testing before dietary or microbiota-targeted strategies can be recommended.

item.title: An Open-Label, Dose-Escalation Trial of Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy for Bipolar II Depression.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This open-label pilot trial assessed the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of psilocybin-assisted therapy for depression in individuals with bipolar II disorder (BD-II).
FINDINGS: Psilocybin (10 mg followed by 25 mg if needed) was well tolerated with no serious adverse events, though transient increases in heart rate/blood pressure and mild-to-moderate side effects (e.g., anxiety, nausea) occurred. Depression scores (MADRS) improved significantly after both doses (10 mg: -12.7 points; 25 mg: -18.6 points), with 28.5% in remission after the 10 mg session. Quality of life (QoL-BD) also improved at 90 days post-treatment.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These preliminary findings suggest psilocybin-assisted therapy may be a viable option for BD-II depression, but larger randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm efficacy and safety.

item.title: Efficacy and safety of esmethadone and rapastinel for major depressive disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the efficacy and safety of esmethadone and rapastinel for major depressive disorder (MDD) in randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
FINDINGS: Across 11 RCTs, neither esmethadone nor rapastinel showed a statistically significant reduction in MADRS scores compared to placebo (MD = -0.62, p = 0.264), and adverse event rates were comparable (RR = 1.09, p = 0.223). Subgroup analyses revealed no significant differences between monotherapy vs. adjunctive therapy or between esmethadone vs. rapastinel.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not support esmethadone or rapastinel as effective treatments for MDD over placebo, though further research may be warranted.

item.title: Efficacy and safety of noninvasive brain stimulation for ADHD: a systematic review and meta-analysis of double-blind randomized controlled trials across international English and Chinese databases.
item.description: BACKGROUND: This meta-analysis and systematic review updates and evaluates the efficacy and safety of non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) techniques for treating clinical symptoms of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), including original studies from China to improve the generalizability of the findings. METHODS: We searched for double-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that assessed the effects of NIBS on clinical ADHD symptoms. Outcomes included clinical symptom improvement, dropout rates, and adverse events.

item.title: Self-Perception of Reproductive Health, Mental Health, and Quality of Life in Females With Classical Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia: A Systematic Review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Classical Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (C-CAH) in females is associated with androgen excess and psychological/physiological masculinization, prompting a systematic review of reproductive self-perception, mental health, and quality of life.
FINDINGS: Across 11 low-bias studies (n=523), females with C-CAH reported atypical gender identity, sexual dissatisfaction, gender dysphoria, and genital virilization concerns. Mental health issues included anxiety, social phobia, ADHD, sexual distress, and depression. Quality of life was reduced, particularly due to general health and pain.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Routine screening for gender dysphoria, sexual dysfunction, and mood/anxiety disorders is warranted in females with C-CAH, alongside multidisciplinary care addressing genital and psychological concerns.

item.title: Long-Read sequencing in psychiatric omics: a systematic review of current evidence.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The comprehensive elucidation of genomic relevance for mental disorder was, until recently, constrained by the limitations of microarrays or short-read sequencing (SRS). Long-read sequencing (LRS) provides access to complex classes of genetic variation and genomic architecture that are largely obscured in SRS approaches, making it a powerful tool for uncovering missing heritability and mechanistic insights in mental disorders. OBJECTIVE: We synthesize current evidence on the application of LRS technologies across genomic, transcriptomic, and methylomic studies of mental disorders.

item.title: Feasibility and acceptability of the Unified Protocol for anxiety and depression in Pakistan: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Access to evidence-based psychological treatments for common mental health disorders remains limited in low-resource settings. This pilot randomized controlled trial evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of the Urdu Adapted Unified Protocol (UA-UP), a transdiagnostic cognitive-behavioral intervention for anxiety and depression, in Pakistan, and explored preliminary clinical outcomes. METHODS: 51 adults meeting diagnostic criteria for anxiety and/or depressive disorders were randomized to a 14-week UA-UP intervention (n=25) or a waitlist control (n=26).

item.title: Effectiveness of amisulpride augmentation versus other antipsychotics in clozapine-treated adolescents: a real-world retrospective study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: In this study, we compared the clinical response to clozapine-amisulpride augmentation versus clozapine augmentation with other antipsychotics among children and adolescents with schizophrenia spectrum disorders in clinical practice. Crucially, the comparative efficacy of specific augmentation strategies in this vulnerable, early-onset population remains a largely unanswered question in current literature.

item.title: Reconceptualizing Schizophrenia through a Patient-Oriented Perspective: a Systematic Review and Qualitative Meta-Synthesis.
item.description: BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders are typically described using positive and negative symptoms, yet standard diagnostic systems may not reflect the full range of how individuals experience the disorder. We hypothesized that synthesizing first-person accounts would yield a broader, clinically useful symptom framework that better represents lived experience. STUDY DESIGN: We performed a systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis following Enhancing Transparency in Reporting the Synthesis of Qualitative Research guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420251069446).

item.title: Comparing the Feasibility of In-Person and Online Preventive Cognitive Therapy for Major Depressive Disorder After Partial Response to Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation: Protocol for a Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: BACKGROUND: In recent years, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has become a first-line recommendation in the Netherlands for individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD) who have not responded to a minimum of 2 prior treatments. Although rTMS can be effective, there is a significant risk of relapse after treatment. Currently, there are no standardized treatment options available after rTMS treatment completion aimed at preventing relapse.

item.title: Brazilian Psychiatric Association Guidelines for the Treatment of Eating Disorders.
item.description: Eating disorders (ED), such as anorexia nervosa (AN), bulimia nervosa (BN), and binge eating disorder (BED), are serious psychiatric conditions that significantly impact psychological and medical health. This paper aims to summarize the recommendations of the Brazilian Association of Psychiatry - [Associação Brasileira de Psiquiatria (ABP)] for the treatment of EDs, based on the latest available evidence. Systematic reviews focused on the multidisciplinary treatment of ED were conducted.

item.title: Gender and other diversity-related factors in psychiatric hospital care: protocol for the participatory mixed-methods PSY-DIVER study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Psychiatric hospital care is multimodal and typically comprises pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, social therapy, occupational therapy, exercise therapy, and various forms of creative therapies. The use, acceptance and effectiveness of these interventions may be shaped by gender and further diversity-related factors including age, migration background, sexual orientation, religious beliefs and socioeconomic status. The impact of such diversity-related factors on psychiatric inpatient care processes and outcomes has not been comprehensively examined in German psychiatric hospitals.

item.title: Utilization of Long-Acting Injectable Antipsychotics and Clozapine in Coordinated Specialty Care: Data From EPINET.
item.description: Objective: We utilized the Early Psychosis Intervention Network (EPINET) platform to examine variability in utilization rates of 2 evidence-based pharmacologic treatments, long-acting injectable (LAI) formulations of antipsychotics and clozapine. Methods: Data come from 8 EPINET clinic consortia, called "hubs," comprising a total of 113 clinics delivering coordinated specialty care (CSC). Hub rates of LAI and clozapine use were calculated based upon the number of patients who were prescribed LAIs or clozapine at any point in a patient's treatment during EPINET participation.

item.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Community-Based Rehabilitation for People With Schizophrenia: A Secondary Analysis of a Cluster Randomized Trial.
item.description: IMPORTANCE: Schizophrenia imposes a substantial disease burden in resource-constrained settings such as China, yet rigorous evidence on the cost-effectiveness of community-based rehabilitation (CBR) remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of a group-based CBR intervention plus facility-based care (FBC) compared with FBC alone for adults with schizophrenia in China.

item.title: A Digital Therapeutic Intervention for Negative Symptoms of Schizophrenia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.description: IMPORTANCE: Negative symptoms of schizophrenia are a major contributor to poor outcomes, yet no US Food and Drug Administration-approved pharmacotherapies are specifically indicated for their treatment. In particular, motivation and pleasure negative symptoms are especially burdensome for patients. Psychosocial interventions can be effective, but access barriers and challenges in sustaining engagement limit their impact. Digital therapeutics are a novel modality that can deliver patient-centered interventions.

item.title: Distinguishing bipolar disorder from unipolar depression in general practice: A systematic review.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Bipolar disorder affects approximately 1% of the population, although some studies report prevalence rates of up to 6%. Distinguishing it from unipolar depression remains challenging, with diagnostic delays often exceeding ten years. This systematic review aims to identify clinical and historical features of depressive episodes that support the earlier detection of bipolar disorder in general practice. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. The PubMed database was searched using MeSH terms.

item.title: Mechanisms of Change in the Treatment of Depression: On the Role of Attachment, Reappraisal and Suppression.
item.description: Identifying mechanisms of change in psychotherapy is imperative to optimize treatment effectiveness for depression. Research has identified specific mechanisms, primarily in outpatient pathology. However, the transdiagnostic robustness of these mechanisms remains to be quantified in more severely affected populations.

item.title: PTSD treatment impacts on pain: secondary analysis of sertraline, prolonged exposure, and their combination.
item.description: Background: Although posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and pain commonly co-occur, interventions often target them separately.

item.title: Maximising the efficacy of in vivo exposure therapy using smartphone-assisted just-in-time adaptive intervention for anxiety disorders: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: For anxiety disorders (ADs), the preferred treatment is cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT), with in vivo exposure (IVE) as its main component. IVE aims to gradually expose the patient to feared stimuli and situations to encourage habituation. Despite its effectiveness, it is a hard component for patients, especially when applied on their own. Therefore, a (co-)therapist usually supports the exposure requiring considerable time and resources. Meanwhile, smartphones have become a promising tool to complement and deliver psychological treatments.

item.title: Mental health burden among survivors of sexual-exploitation trafficking: a global systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression.
item.description: PURPOSE: Survivors of trafficking for sexual exploitation endure sustained violence, coercion and isolation, yet the resulting psychiatric burden has not been reliably quantified across global settings. We aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of mental-health disorders among survivors, to test whether geographical region, exploitation modality or gender explains variation between studies, and to establish how comprehensively the existing literature reports survivors' help-seeking and the structural determinants of their care.

item.title: The immediate and follow-up effects of EMDR therapy for adults with post-traumatic stress disorder: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy is recommended as an effective psychotherapy for adults with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Prior meta-analyses lacked follow-up data or data on comorbid symptoms, and exhibited high heterogeneity. The aims of this meta-analysis were to investigate the immediate and follow-up effects of EMDR on adult patients with PTSD, especially those with comorbid anxiety and depression.

item.title: Bilateral Transcranial Direct-Current Stimulation Over the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex Significantly Reduces Relief Craving During Alcohol Withdrawal: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial Among Inpatients With Alcohol Dependence Syndrome in Northern India.
item.description: Objective: Alcohol dependence syndrome (ADS) carries a heavy global disease burden. Relief craving, the compulsion to drink to escape withdrawal distress, is among its most treatment-resistant features and a frequent trigger for relapse. Given the limited effectiveness of conventional therapies, there is growing interest in targeted neuromodulation of prefrontal circuits as an adjunct approach.

item.title: Perceptions of Technology and Digital Health Tools Among Recently Incarcerated Adults With Opioid Use Disorder: Semistructured Interview Study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Individuals with opioid use disorder (OUD) who return to the community from incarceration face a high risk of fatal drug overdose. This mortality risk is related to significant barriers to accessing health care, social support, and resources needed to transition to and thrive within the community safely. Digital health tools have effectively supported substance use treatment and recovery, but their potential to support OUD during the high-risk period of reentry is underexplored.
